title: Distributed Page Table: Harnessing Physical Memory as an Unbounded Hashed Page Table
problem: Traditional Radix Page Tables (RPTs) have limitations for memory-intensive applications, and Hashed Page Tables (HPTs) face challenges with table resizing and contiguous memory allocation. Address collisions occur when distributed PTEs map to memory locations already allocated to data pages.
motivation: Address translation performance is critical for virtual memory systems, and existing page table designs struggle with the demands of memory-intensive modern applications.
method: DPT distributes page table entries (records that map virtual memory addresses to physical ones) throughout the entire physical memory instead of keeping them in a separate table, eliminating the need to resize the table. When a page table entry would occupy a memory location already holding data (an address collision), three techniques resolve it: Strided Open Addressing (SOA) probes for open space using fixed-size jumps, Collision-Aware Virtual Address Allocation (CVA) guides how data is initially placed to avoid collisions, and Collided Page Displacement (CPD) moves conflicting pages elsewhere in memory.
key_novelty: DPT stores page table entries across the entire physical memory as a distributed hash table, eliminating the need for separate table resizing and reducing collisions.
contributions: Distributed Page Table (DPT) architecture that distributes PTEs across physical memory to eliminate resizing overheads
Three novel address collision resolution techniques: Strided Open Addressing (SOA), Collision-Aware Virtual Address Allocation (CVA), and Collided Page Displacement (CPD)
Experimental validation achieving 12.6% speedup over RPT, 11.6% over large-coverage TLB designs, and 8.7% over state-of-the-art HPTs

metrics.speedup: 12.6% vs RPT, 11.6% vs large-coverage TLB, 8.7% vs state-of-the-art HPTs

primary_theme: Virtual memory optimization through distributed page table design
